outcome: Success rate of labour induction (vaginal delivery within 24 hours)
Time interval from induction to delivery
Maternal outcomes (postpartum hemorrhage, need for blood transfusion, infection)
Neonatal outcomes (Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes, NICU admissions)
cohort: The study included 828 pregnant women requiring labour induction who were randomly assigned to receive either sublingual misoprostol or dinoprostone gel.
finding: Sublingual misoprostol was more effective than dinoprostone gel in achieving vaginal delivery within 24 hours and shortened the time to delivery, though it was associated with a higher incidence of hyperstimulation syndrome.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences between the groups in terms of mode of delivery.
